answer: In this PoA design, each identity posts bonded collateral, but equivocation among k identities is treated as correlated misconduct: the penalty grows as O(k^2), not linearly, through pairwise slash exposure. Detection also applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to the controlling operator, so a sybil swarm rapidly destroys recoverable stake. Thus even a mesa of aliases, a pearl-sized initial bond, or a nadir in detection confidence cannot make mass equivocation economical.
